name: Seoul
summary: Layer royal palaces, hillside hanok streets and night markets across a very efficient metro network. Group Jongno sights together, then spend a separate afternoon on Namsan and Myeongdong.
seasonNote: Spring blossom and autumn colour bring crowds; winter is cold and summer humid with heavy rain.
arrival: From Incheon, take AREX toward Seoul Station; check whether your train is express or all-stop. Gimpo also connects to the metro.
gettingAround: Use a T-money transit card; Naver Map or KakaoMap is useful for local routing. Cluster sights to reduce transfers.
cashTip: Keep won for traditional markets and transit-card top-ups; cards work widely in shops.
foodTip: Try bindaetteok, gimbap and hotteok; ask about pork, seafood and broths if relevant.
buyTip: Compare skincare prices and buy sealed products from established shops; Insadong suits paper and ceramics.
baseArea: Jongno for heritage; Myeongdong for easy transport.

items.name: Mingles
items.summary: Chef Kang Mingoo’s three-star restaurant, a modern take on Korean flavours with a strong focus on fermented sauces.
items.expect: A long tasting-menu meal. Deposits, cancellation fees and smart-casual dress codes are common at this level.
items.tip: Book through the restaurant’s own site or official booking partner as soon as your dates are set.

whyVisit: Chef Kang Mingoo’s three-star restaurant, a modern take on Korean flavours with a strong focus on fermented sauces.
The MICHELIN Guide awards it Three MICHELIN Stars (exceptional cuisine), the guide’s highest award.
visitFlow: Book through the restaurant’s own site or official booking partner as soon as your dates are set.
Share allergies and dietary needs when booking; tasting menus are hard to change on the night.
Allow about three hours and plan a taxi or short walk back.
items.tradeoffs: Among the most expensive meals of a trip, and tables can sell out weeks or months ahead. Menus are set by the kitchen.
